signature.name: Lord Bao Park
signature.detail: The city's best-known sight, a leafy park built around the memorial to Bao Zheng, the incorruptible Song-dynasty official who is a folk hero across China. Come early morning to watch locals doing tai chi, and allow an hour or two to walk the grounds and the memorial halls.

signature.name: Sanhe Ancient Town
signature.detail: A well-preserved water town of old lanes, stone bridges and traditional houses about an hour outside Hefei, the best place nearby to see Anhui's historic architecture. Go on a weekday to avoid crowds and wear comfortable shoes for the cobbled streets.

signature.name: Anhui Museum
signature.detail: The leading museum in the province, strong on Anhui history, calligraphy and regional culture, and a good rainy-day option. It is free to enter with ID, but check opening days since many Chinese museums close on Mondays.

signature.name: Li Hongzhang Former Residence
signature.detail: The family home of Li Hongzhang, the late-Qing statesman, giving a window into 19th-century official life in Hefei. It is compact, so pair it with a walk in the surrounding old streets.

signature.name: Xiaoyaojin Park
signature.detail: A central park with a lake, gardens and a famous name from the Three Kingdoms era, popular with local families. Best in spring and autumn; it is an easy stroll from the city centre.

signature.name: Swan Lake
signature.detail: A modern lakeside area with open views and a skyline backdrop, good for an evening walk. Go around sunset when the light is best and the waterfront is liveliest.

food: Casual meal $5-10; local noodles and snacks cheaper
transport: Metro about $0.5-1 a ride; taxis cheap
